newsitem.title: USA: Great Western may be forced to hold meeting earlier.
newsitem.headline: Great Western may be forced to hold meeting earlier.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp. Monday said a majority of shareholders appeared to support a proposal by H.F. Ahmanson & Co. to force Great Western to hold its annual meeting by May 6.

The Chatsworth, Calif.-based thrift, which is currently the target of a hostile takeover attempt by Ahmanson, said a preliminary review of Ahmanson's consent solicitations showed a majority of Great Western shareholders supported three of five solicitations, including one that would force a shareholder's meeting in May rather than the previously-scheduled date of June 13.
Results for two other solicitations, including one that would force Great Western to negotiate with Ahmanson, are still being tallied.
Later this week, Ahmanson is expected to ask a Delaware Chancery Court judge to order Great Western to change the date for the annual meeting.
In a statement, Ahmanson accused Great Western of dragging its feet and urged the thrift to negotiate with Ahmanson.
"We do not understand the cause for the delay in certification for proposal No. 1, but it appears to be still another example of Great Western stifling its stockholders' voices," Ahmanson said.

"Great Western is running out of excuses for ignoring the will of its stockholders," Ahmanson added. "Stockholders should not have to wait for the additional step of final certification of these results before the Great Western board does the right thing and listens to the true owners of the company."
Great Western has refused to negotiate with Ahmanson, choosing instead to forge a friendly merger with Washington Mutual Inc.. Both bids are worth more than $6 billion.
The company had scheduled its annual meeting for June 13, but Ahmanson has challenged the date and asked a Delaware Chancery Court Judge to order Great Western to hold the meeting sooner.
The unrevoked consents reported in the preliminary count represent approximately 53 percent of Great Western's outstanding shares.
Great Western said the count is preliminary and subject to review and challenge by both Great Western and Ahmanson.

"Great Western's Annual Meeting is scheduled for June 13," the thrift said. "That date was selected by the board as the earliest date that would permit Great Western to comply with the federal proxy rules and ensure that all Great Western stockholders have a sufficient opportunity to receive and review the competing proxy solicitation materials and cast an informed vote."
